entities.summary: Florestano Di Fausto was an Italian architect, engineer and politician who is best known for his building designs in the Italian overseas territories around the Mediterranean. He is considered the most important colonial architect of the Fascist age in Italy and has been described as the "architect of the Mediterranean". Uncontested protagonist of the architectural scene first in the Italian Islands of the Aegean and then in Italian Libya, he was gifted with a remarkable preparation combined with consummate skills, which allowed him to master and to use indifferently and in any geographical context the most diverse architectural styles, swinging between eclecticism and rationalism.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Florestano Di Fausto's architectural designs in Italian overseas territories had a significant regional impact on Mediterranean architecture, influencing local styles and contributing to the development of colonial architecture. His work also reflects the broader cultural and artistic trends of Fascist Italy.
